title: The status message that tr() cannot wrap
summary: QString glued together with + splits the sentence into untranslatable pieces. tr() and arg() keep it whole, and QString::number sets the precision.

turns.user: want to send this to translators so it needs tr(), but it's chopped up with + and I can't wrap it

assistant.body: Sure! When the sentence is cut up with +, a translator only ever sees fragments like Uploaded and of. A language with a different word order cannot translate those. Put the whole sentence in one tr() and leave %1, %2 and %3 for the numbers, filled in by arg(). A translation can then put %2 first if its grammar wants that.

turns.user: seconds come out as 12.3456 s, noisy. one decimal. also chaining arg three times is ugly

assistant.body: Great point! The arg() that takes several values at once is the string version, so the numbers go through QString::number() first, and that is also where the precision goes. It replaces everything in one pass, so a %2 that happens to sit inside an inserted value is never picked up by a later arg().
